description: deixis N[T] identity vectors — structural equality of ADR 0009 §4 (n ≡ m iff D_n = D_m, V_n = V_m, and v_n(p) ≈ v_m(p) on V). Hand-authored from docs/design/0009-optional-node-values.md alone, per vectors/NODE-PLAN.md; not generated by an implementation, and replayed against the four cores by tools/conformance/harness.mjs. Nodes use the N[T] spelling of NODE-PLAN.md over the fixture setoid of vectors/README.md (≈ compares class only). Keys are lowercase hex; "" is the empty key. Under ADR 0010 this file reads as the explicit optional instantiation Node[Option[fixture]], with the tag-respecting option slot of vectors/MNODE-PLAN.md; every case here holds there under the mandatory core's generic laws (checked case by case on 2026-09-23; see NODE-PLAN.md).

cases.name: none-vs-some-empty
cases.note: X3. V_left = {} and V_right = {ε}. None differs from every Some(t), including a payload's own empty value (§4).

cases.name: some-empty-representation-ignored
cases.note: X3/X14. Both are Some; the values agree under ≈, which compares class only (§4 uses the supplied relation).

cases.name: same-class-different-representation-at-depth-two
cases.note: X14. D and V are equal ({ε,[k],[k,j]} and {[k,j]}); the one assigned value agrees under ≈ (§4).

cases.name: different-class-at-root
cases.note: Equal D and V, but v(ε) are not ≈: the classes differ. Same representation on purpose, so native string comparison of representation would wrongly say equal.

cases.name: identical-children-different-own-values
cases.note: X1. §6's counterexample: two parents with identical child maps and different own values. Children alone cannot reconstruct a valued parent. V differs: {ε} vs {}.

cases.name: identical-children-different-own-classes
cases.note: X1. Both parents are valued and have the same children; v(ε) are not ≈.

cases.name: childless-vs-one-empty-child
cases.note: X10. An empty subtree is a real node: D_right = {ε,[k]}, D_left = {ε}. Neither side has a value, so a value-only comparison would wrongly say equal.

cases.name: empty-key-is-a-real-child
cases.note: X5. The empty key is a key: D_left = {ε, [""]}. Empty key and empty path differ (§3).

cases.name: empty-key-vs-zero-byte-key
cases.note: X5. The zero-length key and the one-byte key 0x00 are different byte strings (K = Bytes, §3). A C-string or null-terminated key representation would merge them.

cases.name: keys-differing-only-in-ascii-case
cases.note: C4 (renamed children). 0x6b is 'k' and 0x4b is 'K'. Keys are exact bytes (§3); a case-folding key comparison would wrongly say equal.

cases.name: non-utf8-key-equal-to-itself
cases.note: X5. 0xff00 is not valid UTF-8. Keys are opaque bytes (§3), so a key that fails decoding must still be accepted and must still equal itself.

cases.name: insertion-order-unobservable
cases.note: Sibling order is not a native property beyond keys (§3). Same D and V.

cases.name: value-relocated-to-a-child
cases.note: C2 at the identity level. Same D, same set of values, different V: {ε} vs {[k]}. Placing a parent's value under a child moves it to another native address (§1).

cases.name: payload-class-spelled-none-is-a-value
cases.note: C8. A payload whose class string is "none" is an opaque Some, not the absence tag. T is opaque (§2).

cases.name: payload-class-spelled-some-is-opaque
cases.note: C8. Class strings that look like tags stay payload. The values agree under ≈ (class only).

cases.name: absent-grandchild-vs-empty-grandchild
cases.note: X4/X10. An absent node differs from an existing unvalued node (§4): [k,j] ∈ D_right and not in D_left.

cases.name: valued-vs-unvalued-deep-leaf
cases.note: X3 below the root. V_left = {[k]} and V_right = {}.

cases.name: mixed-tree-reordered-and-rerepresented
cases.note: X1/X5/X14 together. A valued root with children, an unvalued inner node, the empty key, a non-UTF-8 key and Some(empty). Every sibling list is reordered and every representation changed. D and V are equal and every value agrees under ≈.

cases.name: payload-representation-that-spells-a-node-is-still-one-value
cases.note: C8, the other half: a value is not read as structure. The left payload's representation is the literal spelling of the right-hand tree; an implementation that parses payload text as structure would turn left into right. V_left = {ε}, D_right = {ε, [6b]} (§2: T is opaque).

cases.name: payload-representation-is-never-parsed
cases.note: C8. Same class, so ≈ holds; the representation is never consulted, whether or not it happens to spell a node (§4 uses only the supplied relation).
